title: The lesson opens on a familiar outdoor scene where one plant is visibly drooping and one is thriving, inviting the learner to wonder what an individual plant is made of and which parts matter for staying alive. Using a pulled sunflower anchor, the lesson locates and names roots, stem, and leaves, then confronts the beliefs that flowers matter more than roots and that leaves only provide shade. Practice first keeps the labelled structure present while the learner reasons, then removes it, and the lesson closes by checking whether the learner can identify and locate each part in an unlabelled context. (P09 edit)
